text:
cheng: Heads-up — saw a burst of tail latency on prod serving for the MoE route around 11:12UTC. Looks like an all-to-all hotspot on the expert shuffle step. :eyes:

kavi: Do you have a profile flame or nvprof snippet? Was it NCCL or host-side stalls?

cheng: Quick nsight capture attached in thread (pasted below). NCCL alltoall dominates at certain batch shapes, ~45% wall time during step 2. Also observe KV-cache reads spiking when sequence lengths vary a lot.

maria: paste of the heavy part from nsight:
```
# nsight timeline summary (trimmed)
step 2: kernel_compute 22ms | ncclAllToAll 18ms | kernel_compute 5ms | ncclAllToAll 16ms
GPU0 GPU1 GPU2 GPU3 skewed: transfer sizes not even -> multiple small alltoalls
CPU: thread stalls waiting on nccl progress -> no overlap
```

jason: hmm that's the classic expert-shuffle congestion. Are we using the new coalesced routing kernel? Iirc the runtime falls back to non-coalesced for mixed-length batches.

cheng: yes runtime picks coalesced path only when batch shapes align. For mixed shapes we do per-token routing with many little all-to-alls. Profiling shows high kernel launch overhead plus host-side NVLink stalls.

kavi: Two quick ideas: 1) change batching heuristic to group by length modulo a window (coarser bucketing) so more requests hit the coalesced path; 2) force NCCL to use ring/allreduce algorithm that better overlaps with compute (try `NCCL_COLLNET_DISABLE=1` and `NCCL_ALGO=RING` for an A/B).

maria: Also noticing KV cache thrash: when token routing creates many small requests, we lose locality and the local KV cache misses, resulting in repeated device-host transfers. Might help to add a tiny inline prefix cache to route planner (cheap LRU per-GPU).

jason: Agreed. For overlap: we should ensure all-to-all runs on separate CUDA stream with asynchronous progress (enable `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=0` obviously) and call `ncclGroupStart()/ncclGroupEnd()` to batch ops. In my microbenchmarks that reduced apparent alltoall wall time by ~25% when kernels are long.

cheng: Logged an experiment plan:
- A: Coarse length bucketing heuristic (batcher change) -> measure percent coalesced routing vs mixed.
- B: NCCL alg/env tweaks + explicit streams -> microbench wall-time.
- C: Small LRU KV prefetch per-GPU -> KV miss rate.
- D: Fallback kernel selection: prefer compute-bound kernel variant when all-to-all expected to be heavy.

kavi: Can you add perf-bot tags so we get automated traces?

perf-bot: @cheng created perf-run 2026-03-17T11:30Z -> run-id perf-3821. Collecting nsight and nvprof artifacts. :rocket:

maria: One more datapoint — I ran a sim locally with uneven expert fanout and saw NCCL enqueue spikes correlate with small memcpy calls from the routing layer. We should try coalescing those memcpy ops into a single device buffer per GPU.

jason: Good call. Coalesce host->device staging, then kick one alltoall per GPU. Cuts CPU syscall overhead.

cheng: I'll prototype A+B this afternoon on the 8-GPU staging rig. Assigning ownership: batcher + kavi, NCCL/streams + jason, KV prefetch design + maria.

kavi: I'll add the bucketing patch and a toggle flag. If we see >2x coalesced rate it's a win.

maria: I'll sketch LRU prefetch and a small microbench to track device KV hit ratio.

jason: I'll run NCCL alg matrix and async stream changes. Will post microbench numbers.

cheng: Thanks all. If anyone hits a regression, ping #eng-oncall and drop the perf-run id. I'll follow up with a short postmortem note when we have results. :thumbsup:
